profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI (also known as Ai2) is a nonprofit AI research laboratory founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, WA. The organization describes itself as conducting high-impact research and engineering to tackle key problems in artificial intelligence, guided by open, collaborative, and inclusive principles aimed at producing safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems. Its site notes partnerships with the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering, the National Science Foundation on an open multimodal AI infrastructure project, and Google Cloud in support of open model development and scientific research platforms.

Ai2 is led by Ali Farhadi and places particular emphasis on fully open AI, meaning its research outputs and training data are made publicly available. Among its notable work, the organization applies AI to environmental and scientific challenges including climate science, agriculture, wildfire management, and wildlife protection. Its two tracked products are OLMo, an open-source large language model developed with full transparency into training data, and Semantic Scholar, an AI-powered academic search tool offering paper summaries and citation graphs oriented toward the research community.

The held facts list no litigation or regulatory filings associated with Ai2, and no MCP server presence is recorded. The organization is verified as a nonprofit research lab, consistent with how it presents itself on its own site.
